UNCERTAINTY AND LONG-TERM PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT OF CONSTRICTION-TYPE FLOW MEASUREMENT STRUCTURES FOR SUSTAINABLE IRRIGATION WATER MANAGEMENT

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: A.A. Naumova

Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.01.2026.384.391

ABSTRACT

Accurate flow measurement is essential for sustainable irrigation water management, directly affecting water distribution efficiency, equitable allocation, and resource conservation. This study presents a systematic GUM-compliant (ISO/IEC Guide 98-3) uncertainty analysis of three constriction-type measurement structures widely deployed in Central Asian irrigation networks: Venturi flumes, Parshall flumes, and SANIIRI nozzles. A sensitivity-based uncertainty propagation framework was applied to quantify the individual and combined contributions of five uncertainty sources: upstream water level measurement, throat geometry, discharge coefficient calibration, fluid properties, and hydraulic approach conditions. At design-flow conditions (coverage factor k = 2, confidence level p = 95 %, design head h = 0.50 m), combined expanded uncertainties are: 2.9% (Venturi flume), 4.6% (Parshall flume), and 5.3% (SANIIRI nozzle). Discharge coefficient calibration is the dominant uncertainty source for Parshall flumes (weighted contribution 2.00 % vs. 0.91 % for water level) and co-primary for Venturi flumes. Venturi and Parshall flumes satisfy the ISO 4359:2022 accuracy requirement of Uᵣ(Q) ≤ 5 %; SANIIRI nozzles marginally exceed this threshold (Uᵣ = 5.3 %) and require individual laboratory calibration for compliant operation. A multi-mechanism concrete degradation model integrating carbonation (kᶜ = 1 mm/year⁻¹), freeze-thaw cycling (kᶠᵗ = 0.005 mm/cycle, Nᶜʸ = 80 cycles/year), and sediment abrasion (kₐᵇ = 0.05 mm·m³·kg⁻¹·year⁻¹) was developed to project measurement accuracy over a 30-year operational horizon under three maintenance scenarios. Without maintenance, combined uncertainty exceeds the 5 % ISO 4359:2022 threshold within approximately 7 years and reaches 8.6 % by year 30, representing a 72 % exceedance of the regulatory limit. A 5-year geometric restoration cycle (Scenario A) maintains time-averaged expanded uncertainty at 4.7 %, ensuring continuous compliance over the full service life. Cross-regional comparison with four irrigation systems (Fergana Valley, Uzbekistan; lower Syr Darya, Kazakhstan; Punjab canals, Pakistan; Yellow River basin, China) validates the model predictions across the full range of maintenance regimes. The findings provide quantitative guidance for maintenance scheduling, device selection, and accuracy specification in large-scale irrigation projects, contributing to sustainable irrigation water management.
